sources.entry: OneCLI | Credential vault for AI agents — Rust HTTP gateway injects API keys transparently so agents never handle raw secrets

summary.one_liner: OneCLI is an open-source platform for running sandboxed AI agents for teams, with a Rust gateway that injects credentials so agents never handle raw API keys.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OneCLI v2 as a platform where you create one sandboxed agent per employee and grant each agent specific access. Outbound agent traffic goes through a Rust gateway that intercepts HTTPS via MITM, injects credentials, and enforces team policy. Secrets are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM and matched by host and path pattern. The stack includes a Next.js dashboard, an API control plane with a database and work queue, a runner that starts and reaps sandboxes, an SSH terminator using short-lived certificates, and a Slack channel adapter with one app per agent. Human-in-the-loop approvals and shared team-level connections are also described. Self-hosting uses pnpm, with a Helm chart for Kubernetes.
use_cases: keep API keys away from autonomous agents
self-host a credential vault for AI agents
run agents in Slack with per-agent identity
approve risky agent actions before they run
manage shared LLM keys across a team
how_to_run: Local dev: mise install && pnpm install && pnpm dev
notable: Gateway injects credentials into outbound HTTPS requests so agents never see raw secrets
Integrates with Bitwarden or 1Password for on-demand credential injection with nothing stored on the server
Runner is outbound-only with no inbound ports, so it works behind NAT
Deterministic human-in-the-loop approvals in chat for sensitive actions
Enterprise features live in ee/ directories under a separate license
caveats: Enterprise paths under ee/ require a subscription for production use
Contributions require accepting a Contributor License Agreement
Multi-component setup (dashboard, API server, gateway, runner, PostgreSQL) for self-hosting
